q: Which structural formula represents butan-2-ol?
explain: Butan-2-ol has four carbons in a chain with the –OH group on carbon 2. CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH is butan-1-ol.

q: Which fraction from the fractionating column has the lowest boiling points?
explain: Refinery gas contains the smallest molecules, so it has the lowest boiling points and is collected at the top.

q: A sample of poly(ethene) has a relative molecular mass of 28 000. How many ethene units, C₂H₄, are in each molecule?
explain: The relative molecular mass of C₂H₄ is 28, so the number of units is 28 000 ÷ 28 = 1000.

q: Which row correctly describes the reaction of ethane and ethene with aqueous bromine?
explain: Only the unsaturated alkene, ethene, decolourises aqueous bromine. Ethane is saturated and causes no change.

q: Which compound is a saturated hydrocarbon?
explain: C₄H₁₀ is butane, an alkane with only single bonds. C₄H₈ and C₃H₆ are alkenes and C₂H₅OH is not a hydrocarbon.

q: Which row correctly describes the manufacture of ethanol by the addition of steam to ethene?
options: hydration of ethene | glucose | acid catalyst
hydration of ethene | ethene and steam | acid catalyst
explain: Hydration uses ethene and steam with an acid catalyst. Fermentation uses aqueous glucose with yeast.

q: Which compound is a carboxylic acid?
explain: Carboxylic acids contain the –COOH functional group. CH₃CH₂COOH is propanoic acid.

q: A chain in a protein is made from 5 amino acid molecules joined together. How many water molecules are formed?
explain: Joining n monomers in a chain makes n – 1 links, and each link forms with the loss of one water molecule. For 5 amino acids that is 4 water molecules.

q: Why do members of the same homologous series have similar chemical properties?
options: They have the same relative molecular mass.
They have the same functional group.
They have the same number of carbon atoms.
They have the same physical state at room temperature.
explain: The functional group determines how a compound reacts, and every member of a series has the same one.

q: Which pair of compounds reacts to form the ester propyl methanoate?
explain: The first part of the name (propyl) comes from the unbranched alcohol propan-1-ol, and the second part (methanoate) comes from methanoic acid.

q: Which fraction is used for lubricants, waxes and polishes?
explain: Lubricating oil has long, viscous molecules suitable for lubricants, waxes and polishes.

q: Which reaction is an addition reaction?
explain: In C₂H₄ + Br₂ → C₂H₄Br₂ two molecules join to form one product. The other reactions are substitution, combustion and cracking.

q: Which pair of monomers could form a polyamide?
explain: A polyamide needs a dicarboxylic acid and a diamine. A diol with a dicarboxylic acid would give a polyester.

q: Which poisonous gas can form when an alkane burns in a limited supply of oxygen?
explain: Incomplete combustion produces carbon monoxide, which is toxic, and sometimes carbon (soot).

q: 4.6 g of ethanol, C₂H₅OH, burns completely. What volume of carbon dioxide is formed at room temperature and pressure? (Mᵣ of ethanol = 46; 1 mole of gas occupies 24 dm³ at r.t.p.)
explain: 4.6 ÷ 46 = 0.10 mol ethanol. C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O gives 0.20 mol CO₂, and 0.20 × 24 = 4.8 dm³.

q: 25.0 cm³ of sodium hydroxide of concentration 0.200 mol/dm³ is exactly neutralised by ethanoic acid. How many moles of ethanoic acid react?
explain: Moles of NaOH = 0.0250 dm³ × 0.200 mol/dm³ = 5.00 × 10⁻³ mol. The reaction is 1 : 1, so 5.00 × 10⁻³ mol of acid reacts.

q: How do the boiling points of the alkanes change as the number of carbon atoms increases?
options: They increase for odd numbers of carbon atoms only.
explain: Physical properties show a trend along a homologous series. Longer molecules have stronger forces between them, so boiling points rise.

q: Which row correctly describes ethanol?
explain: Ethanol (name ending -ol) is an alcohol with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH and the –OH functional group.

q: Which fraction contains the molecules with the longest hydrocarbon chains?
explain: Bitumen has the longest chains, the highest boiling point and the highest viscosity, so it condenses at the bottom of the column.

q: Why is it a problem to burn waste plastics to avoid using landfill sites?
options: The burning can produce toxic gases.
The plastics burn to make metal.
The plastics melt to form fuels.
explain: Burning avoids landfill but some plastics release toxic gases, so it can cause air pollution.

q: A colourless gas is bubbled through aqueous bromine and the solution stays orange. Which could be the gas?
explain: Only unsaturated compounds decolourise aqueous bromine. Ethane is saturated, so there is no reaction.

q: A plastic is not biodegradable. Which statement about its disposal is correct?
options: It rots in landfill within a few weeks.
It is broken down by bacteria in the soil.
It stays in landfill for a very long time.
explain: Microorganisms cannot break it down, so a non-biodegradable plastic stays unchanged in landfill for a very long time.

q: Propane reacts with chlorine in ultraviolet light. Which formula is that of a monosubstitution product?
explain: A monosubstitution product has one H replaced by one Cl: C₃H₇Cl. CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl is 1-chloropropane. The others have a double bond or more than one Cl.

q: Why is ethanol made by fermentation of sugar cane used as a fuel in some countries?
options: The sugar cane can be regrown, so the raw material is renewable.
It burns to form no carbon dioxide.
explain: Sugar cane is a plant raw material that can be regrown each year, unlike petroleum.

q: Which row correctly describes the reaction of ethanoic acid with magnesium?
explain: Magnesium releases hydrogen from ethanoic acid and forms magnesium ethanoate. Carbon dioxide is released only by carbonates.

q: How many hydrogen atoms are in one molecule of propanol, C₃H₇OH?
explain: Seven hydrogen atoms are in the C₃H₇ group and one is in the –OH group, giving 8.

q: Which compound is named ethane?
explain: Ethane is the alkane with two carbon atoms joined by a single bond, CH₃CH₃. CH₂=CH₂ is ethene.

q: Going down the fractionating column, how do the volatility and viscosity of the fractions change?
explain: Lower down, the chains are longer, so the fractions are less volatile and flow less easily (higher viscosity).

q: Ethene reacts with steam to make ethanol: C₂H₄ + H₂O → C₂H₅OH. What mass of ethanol forms from 14 g of ethene, assuming all the ethene reacts?
explain: Mᵣ of C₂H₄ = 28 and of C₂H₅OH = 46. 14 g is 0.50 mol, which forms 0.50 mol of ethanol: 0.50 × 46 = 23 g.

q: Which row correctly describes PET?
options: polyamide | amide link | dicarboxylic acid and diol
polyester | ester link | dicarboxylic acid and diol
polyester | ester link | dicarboxylic acid and diamine
polyamide | amide link | dicarboxylic acid and diamine
explain: PET is a polyester, so it has ester links and forms from a dicarboxylic acid and a diol.
